newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: WHITLAM WEEPS OVER COFFIN OF DEPUTY
Former Labor Prime Minister Gough Whitlam wept over the coffin of the man who was his deputy in Launceston today.
Mr Whitlam was among dozens of figures from boths sides and all levels of politics at the State Funeral of the man he called his right arm and most loyal mate, Lance Barnard.
Mr Barnard died in Melbourne last week after undergoing heart surgery, aged 78.
Mr Whitlam delivered a euology praising his deputy's contribution through a turbulent parliamentary period.
But it was the image of Mr Barnard's volunteer war service in the Middle East that moved Mr Whitlam.
FORMER TAX COMMISSIONER QUESTIONS PM'S TAX CUT PROMISE
Former Tax Commissioner Trevor Boucher has questioned the Prime Minister's promise to reduce personal income tax as part of the Government's re-shaping of the tax system.

Mr Boucher, who's taking part in a separate review of the tax system organised by the Evatt Foundation, said a certain level of tax was needed to ensure Governments can provide essential infrastructure.
He said there was a growing gap between what the community expected from Governments and what they were prepared to pay in tax.
Mr Boucher said Governments had to date been able to rely on contributions from asset sales to improve their budget positions, but this could not last forever and the tax base needed to be protected.
DYING WOMAN ORDERED TO REPAY COMPENSATION
New South Wales' highest court has ordered a Sydney woman dying of breast cancer to repay half a million dollars in compensation.
Kathryn Curtin, 32, was awarded $524,000 by the New South Wales Supreme Court after she sued her general practitioner and her endocrinologist for negligence.
Ms Curtin claimed that they did not treat her breast cancer, which metastasised into her liver and reduced her life expectancy.
The New South Wales Court of Appeal has today upheld an appeal by the medical practitioners, meaning the woman will have to return the money and pay their legal costs.
Outside the court, Kathryn Curtin said some of the money has already been spent on her medical bills.
BORDER PRAISES VICTORIOUS CRICKET TEAM
Former Australian cricket captain Allan Border says our current team deserves to be regarded as the best in the world.
Speaking at the launch of the book "200 seasons of Australian cricket" at the MCG, Border said Mark Taylor had done enough to hold onto the captaincy, for the time being.
